label: 3rd original token right after an early i (x-i-_ prefix), for some first tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely at t=2 (94% of mass; small tails at t=1 and t=3). Never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The main trigger is the 3rd input when the 2nd input was i (prev_tok=i holds 87% of mass). It also needs the first token to be in a particular, fairly arbitrary set (a,c,d,i,l,m,o,r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y,0,2). After b,e,f,g,h,j,k,n,p,q,z,1,3 followed by i, it essentially never fires. A smaller second clause is d at t=1 when the first token is i or d (e.g. i d _, d d _). Magnitude: the strongest activations (the max, 2.34) all come from the prefix d i s, and first tokens d/i give higher values. Weak tails (about 6% of mass): s at t=1 after an initial i (about 0.14 of max), and t=3 after i i or d i. Dev split: P=0.96, R=0.88, mass recall 0.94.

issues: All main claims check out on dev. The feature fires only in the original phase: 0 activations at the delimiter, in the copy phase, at t=0 and at t>=4. Activation mass by position is t=2 0.941, t=1 0.027, t=3 0.032. prev_tok=i holds 0.875 of the mass. All of the top activations (2.339) are on the prefix d i s.
The first-token set is real and sharp. At t=2 after i, the listed first tokens give P=0.955 and the excluded ones give P=0.0056.

The explanation misdescribes the second clause. It says 'd at t=1 when the first token is i or d'. The predicate actually fires at t=2, on the 3rd token after 'i d' or 'd d' (P=1.0, mass recall 0.123).

The tails are as described, but the predicate leaves them out, and they are systematic rather than scattered noise. 'i s' at t=1 has P=1.0 and recall 0.050. The t=3 step after 'x i i' or 'x d i' has P=0.63 and recall 0.058. Together they cause most of the missed activations.
There is a minor systematic false-positive group: 'x i d' at t=2 has P=0.61 even when the first token is in the set. It covers only about 1.7% of recall and was left as is.
